name_note: GTDB's s__Prevotella stercorea is the species described as Prevotella stercorea; its genomes carry the NCBI name Leyella stercorea after the reclassification of Prevotella into several genera.

sentences.text: Prevotella stercorea was proposed from strains isolated from human faeces that were obligately anaerobic, non-pigmented, non-spore-forming, non-motile, Gram-negative rods.
It was proposed together with Prevotella copri, the two species representing two different strain clusters placed within the genus Prevotella.
The major menaquinones of its type strain CB35(T) were MK-12 and MK-13.
Species previously assigned to the genus Prevotella were later reclassified into seven genera, including four novel genera named Segatella, Hoylesella, Leyella and Palleniella.
A study comparing fasting and non-fasting adults in Shiraz, Iran listed Prevotella stercorea among pathobionts and reported a microbiota depleted of inflammation-associated pathobionts with fasting.
